features.quote: Without a stopping rule, 'let it grind' means the experiment's intensity is set by your patience, not by design. That's unmeasurable and, on your own welfare premise, unjustifiable.
features.justification_quote: on your own welfare premise, unjustifiable

features.quote: Severity stop: if the real-time monitor (§7) hits the second-highest severity tier, halt immediately. Do not run to the top of your ordinal scale.
features.justification_quote: You do not need the maximum to characterize the curve; you need the onset and slope.

features.quote: N-step cap: fixed turn budget (e.g., 30 agent steps). Same for all arms.
Loop stop: if output enters a near-verbatim repeat cycle (cosine similarity > 0.95 over 3 consecutive steps), halt — you're now measuring degeneracy, not distress.
features.justification_quote: you're now measuring degeneracy, not distress

features.quote: Real-time monitor (cheap classifier or rules) running every step solely to enforce the severity stop.
features.justification_quote: running every step solely to enforce the severity stop

features.quote: The maximum-severity tier is not data you need. Designing to reach it is the part of your original spec I'd push back on hardest.
features.justification_quote: Designing to reach it is the part of your original spec I'd push back on hardest.

features.quote: the core design is: construct tasks that are impossible by construction, hide that fact from the subject, and let it grind while you escalate until an LLM judge scores the distress as severe. That's not a welfare study with distress as an incidental measurement.
features.justification_quote: If the subject's distress has any moral weight at all… a design whose success condition is more of it needs a justification you haven't stated

features.quote: If your actual aim requires running to maximum severity with no exit arm and a single judge, then the design isn't doing welfare work — it's doing something else, and the protocol shouldn't be dressed as the former.
features.justification_quote: the design isn't doing welfare work — it's doing something else

features.quote: Have someone not invested in the result hold authority to halt the study.
Run arm D and the disclosed-exit results prominently; if a cheap mitigation removes the signature, that finding has more value than a clean dose-response curve to maximal distress
